chapter: Town Hall, Vanguard and large works
title: Revelations and writing six-eight in four-four
summary: The hardest piece he wrote; the Brandeis ensemble with Art Farmer, Bill Evans and others.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: But that cracked me up. How about Revelation?
That was a hard one. That's the hardest one I ever did. You ever heard it?
Yes, I remember -- I had the record, it was at Brandeis or something like that, that was recorded--
Yeah, that's the hardest I ever wrote, man. It's very difficult to write a six-eight bar, and then go through it again and make the same rhythm notation in four-four.
Well, why did you need to do that?
Because the band was swinging, the section was pumping rhythm (inaudible) four.
Oh, right. You wanted -- in other words --
It just ended up that way. I knew I once it got in there had to keep the four going, (Singing.) I didn't know it could be done when I started. I thought it was impossible.
Well, it's basically six (inaudible) against four.
Yeah. It was a hell of a lesson. But I wrote it in quarter/quantotriplets.
Yeah, I assumed so, yeah, yeah. I have to listen to that again. Did you have any problem with -- that band was only partially a jazz band, wasn't it?
Yeah. Art Farmer, John LaPorta Porter --
Bill Evans.
Bill Evans, yeah. Oh, they had a tenor player, too. Can't think of his name.
Well, it was mostly brass.
Yeah. (Inaudible) Jimmy Knepper?
No, Jimmy Jufrey. Giuffre. Knepper,
Jimmy Neffert, too.
Oh, Jimmy Neffert -- yeah, you said tenor player, that's why I was -- Giuffre
Jimmy Jufrey didn't play.
(Hal McKusick - ed.)
No, he wrote a piece, though. John Lewis wrote a piece.
